root_cause.text: The MPLS netns code updated the related `net->mpls.platform_labels` size and `net->mpls.platform_label` RCU pointer without a single reader-visible consistency mechanism, allowing RCU readers in `mpls_forward`, `mpls_dump_routes`, and `mpls_label_ok` to observe a mismatched pair during table resize and index past bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “RCU-protected codepaths (mpls_forward, mpls_dump_routes) can have an inconsistent view of platform_labels vs platform_label in case of a concurrent resize ... This can lead to OOB accesses,” and the patch fixes this by adding `seqcount_mutex_t platform_label_seq`, wrapping writer updates with `write_seqcount_begin/end()`, and making readers fetch both values through `mpls_platform_label_rcu()` with `read_seqcount_begin/retry()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a seqcount-with-mutex field to netns_mpls to support synchronized access tracking for platform label state.
intent_record.what: A new field named platform_label_seq of type seqcount_mutex_t was added to struct netns_mpls, immediately after the existing platform_mutex member.
intent_record.how: This extends the MPLS network namespace state with a sequence counter associated with the platform label mutex, enabling code to track or synchronize concurrent access to platform label data using seqcount-with-mutex semantics at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix MPLS RCU route lookup to read the platform label array and its size consistently and avoid races during bounds checking.
intent_record.what: A new helper function, mpls_platform_label_rcu(struct net *net, size_t *platform_labels), is added to read net->mpls.platform_label and net->mpls.platform_labels together under a seqcount retry loop using read_seqcount_begin/read_seqcount_retry and rcu_dereference. In mpls_route_input_rcu(), a local size_t platform_labels variable is introduced, the new helper is called to obtain both the platform_label pointer and label count, the bounds check is changed from net->mpls.platform_labels to the local platform_labels value, and the direct rcu_dereference(net->mpls.platform_label) is removed.
intent_record.how: This makes mpls_route_input_rcu() use a consistent snapshot of the platform_label array pointer and its size during RCU lookup. It prevents races where the label count and array pointer could be observed from different update states, which could otherwise lead to an invalid bounds check and unsafe array access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a shared helper to retrieve MPLS platform label state instead of open-coding separate accesses.
intent_record.what: Two separate assignments that read `net->mpls.platform_label` via `rcu_dereference()` and `net->mpls.platform_labels` directly were replaced with a single call to `mpls_platform_label_rcu(net, &platform_labels)` that returns the platform label pointer and fills `platform_labels` through an output parameter.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this consolidates retrieval of the MPLS platform label table pointer and label count into one helper, likely ensuring they are obtained in a coordinated RCU-safe manner instead of through separate field accesses that could become inconsistent or duplicated across call sites.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect platform label table resize updates with bottom-half disabling and seqcount writes so readers cannot see inconsistent label table state.
intent_record.what: The change wraps the update of net->mpls.platform_labels and the RCU assignment to net->mpls.platform_label with local_bh_disable()/local_bh_enable() and write_seqcount_begin()/write_seqcount_end() using net->mpls.platform_label_seq.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the platform label table pointer-and-size update execute as a protected synchronized write-side critical section, preventing readers from observing an inconsistent combination of table pointer and label limit during resize and coordinating safely with seqcount-based readers in bottom-half contexts.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the MPLS platform label seqcount with its mutex during network namespace setup to ensure correct synchronization.
intent_record.what: A call to seqcount_mutex_init(&net->mpls.platform_label_seq, &net->mpls.platform_mutex) was added in mpls_net_init() immediately after mutex_init(&net->mpls.platform_mutex).
intent_record.how: This initializes the platform_label_seq seqcount and associates it with platform_mutex during MPLS per-network namespace setup, enabling correct sequence-count based synchronization for later readers and writers and preventing use of an uninitialized synchronization primitive at runtime.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix MPLS platform label table synchronization by using seqcount-protected reads, writes, and proper initialization to avoid races and inconsistent route lookup state.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is lack of a single reader-visible consistency mechanism when updating platform_labels and platform_label. Adding a seqcount-with-mutex to netns_mpls directly introduces synchronization to track and validate consistent reads of that state during resize/update.

The changes directly address the root cause: inconsistent reader-visible updates of `platform_labels` size and `platform_label` pointer during MPLS table resize. Adding seqcount-protected reads/writes and proper seqcount initialization provides the missing consistency mechanism for RCU readers and prevents mismatched size/pointer observations and out-of-bounds access.

The root cause is inconsistent reader-visible access to the MPLS platform_labels size and platform_label pointer. Replacing open-coded separate accesses with a shared helper directly targets how readers obtain that state and is relevant to preventing mismatched reads during resize.

candidates.rationale: This write updates the visible size independently of the RCU pointer update, creating the inconsistent reader-visible pair at the heart of the race.
This write updates the table pointer separately from the size field, so readers can observe a new pointer with an old size or vice versa and index incorrectly.
This bounds check reads platform_labels without synchronizing with the paired platform_label pointer read, allowing a stale/mismatched size to validate an index for a different table.
This pointer read is performed separately from the size read, so the reader may fetch a table that does not correspond to the previously checked platform_labels value.
This unsynchronized read of the table size in dump code can be paired with a different-generation platform_label pointer, matching the root cause described for mpls_dump_routes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement updates the visible platform label table size independently of the paired RCU pointer update, creating the reader-visible inconsistency that allows RCU readers to observe a mismatched size/pointer pair during resize.
This statement updates the platform label table pointer separately from the size field, so readers can observe a new pointer with an old size or an old pointer with a new size and index past bounds.

This bounds check reads platform_labels without synchronization with the corresponding platform_label pointer read, allowing validation of an index against a size that may belong to a different table instance.
This pointer read is done separately from the platform_labels size read, so the reader can fetch a table that does not correspond to the size used for bounds checking.

This unsynchronized read of the platform label table size in dump code can be paired with a different-generation platform_label pointer, reproducing the same inconsistent size/pointer race in mpls_dump_routes.
